run: P4' fair re-test on the SAVED checkpoints of seeds 0, 1, 2; forward passes only, NO training

model.note: 1 layer: tokens (a, b, '=') with '=' = id 113; causal attention (no biases on Q/K/V/O), MLP W_in+b_in -> ReLU -> W_out+b_out, residual stream only (no LayerNorm), unembed (no bias) read at the '=' position (index 2) -> logits over 113 classes = (a+b) mod 113. Init: W_E, W_pos ~ N(0, 1/d_model); Linear layers PyTorch default

split_def: all 113*113 pairs (a, b), index a*113+b; numpy default_rng(split_seed).permutation; first floor(0.3*12769) = 3830 = train, the rest (8939) = held-out test
sweep_def: for each b in b_set: inputs (a, b, '=') for a = 0..112; read the MLP post-ReLU activations (512) at the '=' position -> acts (5, 113, 512) float32, saved
pipeline: IMPORTED unchanged from osc_neuron_period2.py: dpeak (= detrend over span{1, a} then run 1's peakiness) and detrended_null; peakiness = max non-DC rfft power / total non-DC power over the 113-long a series, dominant bin k in 1..56
statistic: per neuron: detrended peakiness per b, averaged over the 5 b -> pk; dominant frequency k = the most common per-b dominant bin over the 5 b (ties -> smallest k)
null_def: detrended label-shuffled null: for each b, osc_neuron_period2.detrended_null(acts_b, 20, null_seed) (permute a FIRST, then detrend, then peakiness; the same 20 permutations for every b) -> (20, 512) per b, averaged over b -> pooled 10240 values, 99.9th pct
twin_def: random-init twin: the SAME architecture built after torch.manual_seed(twin_seed), untrained, same sweep and statistic; null 2 = max pk over its 512 neurons
p1_set: neurons with pk > null q999 AND pk > twin max (both strict); fraction over all 512
p2_def: dominant frequencies of the P1 neurons sorted by count (desc, ties smallest k); n_cover = the fewest of them whose counts sum to >= 0.8 * |P1|; pass = |P1| > 0 and n_cover <= 6
box_stop: training checks memory PSI some avg10 at each eval; >= 20 -> checkpoint and exit 3 (resumable)
threads_note: 1 while the post unit's tracer is on (TracerPid non-zero), per the order; <= 4 otherwise
rng: numpy default_rng([u_seed or n_seed, model_seed, family_k]); U: 200 uniform size-matched sets over ALL 512 neurons; N: size-matched sets drawn uniformly over all 512, ACCEPTED iff |mean W_out column norm of the set - the family's| <= norm_window, until 200 accepted or max_draws
norm_def: W_out column norm = L2 norm of model.w_out.weight[:, i] (the 128-vector neuron i writes to the residual stream); a set's norm = the mean over its neurons
load_bearing_def: a family (>= family_floor neurons from the imported PC pipeline) is LOAD-BEARING iff its mean-ablation held-out accuracy drop is STRICTLY greater than np.quantile(U drops, 0.99) AND np.quantile(N drops, 0.99); a family with fewer than n_sets accepted N sets in max_draws is N-UNTESTABLE: reported, and it cannot be load-bearing (the AND cannot be satisfied)
percentile_report: per family: pU = pct of the 200 U drops <= the family's drop, pN likewise (unscored)
ablation: the imported S.evaluate with abl=(mask, means), means = model.seen.mean(0) over all 12769 inputs at '=', scored on the held-out split (S.data split_seed 0); families from S.sweep/S.stat/S.null + T.families with the PC thresholds, unchanged
verdict_rule: VOID (checked first) if a checkpoint sha256 differs from checkpoints[...].sha256 or a seed's held-out accuracy (baseline, no ablation) < 0.99. Else C1 = every seed in model_seeds has >= 1 load-bearing family: C1 -> proved, any seed without one -> disproved. params.json sha256 recorded at launch must equal the final one, else void
unscored: per family pU / pN; count of load-bearing families per seed; whether seed 0's labels (k=5, k=45 load-bearing; k=1, k=34 passengers) survive P4' (each family: load-bearing yes/no under P4')
